doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Cuban Bennett's career, style and death
summary: Discussion of Cuban's New York career in the mid-twenties, his never recording, how Carter would liken his style to Clifford Brown, and uncertainty over when he died.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What did he do in New York? He certainly didn’t play in any of the known big bands. Did he support himself solely as a musician?
Oh yes. Yes, he never did anything else but play music. I don’t know. He never played with any of the big bands. I don’t remember. This was in the mid-twenties.
By that time you were already sort of in your, you might call, it apprentice period.
Yes, and unfortunately I never played with him.
Never.
No. I don’t know. I can’t explain at this particular time why.
He seems to have been outside the mainstream, if you can use that word.
Yeah, that’s the way it seems.

About his style, I mean, it’s hard, of course, to describe it to someone who’s never heard it, and as you said, there are no records. But people like, as you mentioned, Roy Eldridge, and I think Rex Stewart mentions him.
Rex Stewart, of course.
Said he was doing things in the twenties . . . I think they maybe oversimplified it, but said he was like playing bebop in the twenties.
Well, I wouldn’t call it bebop, but . . .
Or some of the things that . . .
I would liken his sound and his style more to a sort of a Clifford Brown, which I guess some people would call bebop, but not to that extent. I wouldn’t have called it bebop then, nor would I now.
Did he talk to you about music? Did he show you anything on the horn?

Not too much. He was sort of a loner, and, I might add, he was sort of a tippler. That may have had something to do with his not playing with other groups that I knew of. But he used to play at the clubs around New York, mainly in Harlem. But I don’t know that he ever played with a band.
Did he continue to play? I think he died at the age of sixty-three or something.
Gee, I didn’t think he died that old. I thought he died much younger.
Anyway, he died in 1965.
Nineteen when?
’65? Are you sure?
I think so.
Oh, I don’t think he was around until ’65.
No?
No.
He was five years older than you, I believe.
Probably, yeah.
So as far as you know . . . well, if he did, I can check the date, but . . .
Gee, I . . . oh, I think . . .
But he was certainly not active in music [unclear].
No, he wasn’t active. I think he even moved to Philadelphia or something. But, gee, I don’t think he died in ’65.
Really.
Well, I’d have to check with the family to find out, you know. There are those that know, you know, still in McDonald.
